cards.text: Ezekiel the prophet has sat among the exiles at Tel-abib by the River Kebar for seven days, overwhelmed (Ezekiel 3:15). At the end of those seven days the word of the LORD comes: "Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel." Seven days of sitting, then BAM, a brand new job title, no interview, no paperwork, friend, NOTHING.

cards.question: Ezekiel is now Israel's watchman. Whenever he hears a word from God's mouth, what is he supposed to give the people?

cards.text: Then God walks him through it, case by case. Case one: say God tells a wicked man, "You will surely die," and Ezekiel doesn't warn him.

cards.question: In case one, God tells a wicked man he will surely die. True or false: if Ezekiel stays quiet, that wicked man gets a pass because Ezekiel never warned him.
When the unwarned wicked man dies in his iniquity, God will hold ___ responsible for his blood.

cards.text: Case two: say Ezekiel DOES warn the wicked man, and the man won't turn from his wickedness and his wicked way. He will die in his iniquity.

cards.question: In case two, Ezekiel warned the wicked man, but the man wouldn't turn. Where does that leave Ezekiel?

cards.text: Case three flips it: say a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and God puts a stumbling block before him. If Ezekiel didn't warn him, he will die in his sin, and that line again: God will hold Ezekiel responsible for his blood.

cards.question: In case three, a righteous man turned to sin and was never warned. True or false: the righteous acts he did will still be remembered.
Case four: Ezekiel warns a righteous man not to sin, and the man doesn't sin. What happens to that man?

answers.text: He will die in his sin
He is cut off from Israel

cards.text: He will indeed live because he heeded the warning, and Ezekiel will have saved himself. FINALLY, a case where I can unclench my mustache.
With the hand of the LORD upon him, Ezekiel gets up and goes out to the plain as God says, and there is the glory of the LORD, like the glory he saw by the River Kebar.

cards.question: True or false: with the glory of the LORD right there on the plain, Ezekiel falls facedown.

cards.text: Then the Spirit enters him and sets him on his feet. Facedown one minute, back on his feet the next: this prophet is getting his steps in.

cards.question: Back on his feet, Israel's new watchman gets his next order from God. Where does God send him?

answers.text: Into his house to shut himself in
Up onto the city wall to watch

cards.text: Then God tells him, "And you, son of man, they will tie with ropes, and you will be bound so that you cannot go out among the people." A watchman stuck in the house, and friend, I did years in a junk drawer and nobody even bothered with ropes.

cards.question: God says He'll make Ezekiel's tongue stick to the roof of his mouth. What will that keep Ezekiel from doing?

cards.text: God says Ezekiel will be silent, though the people are a rebellious house. But God says when He speaks with him, He will open his mouth, and Ezekiel is to tell them, "This is what the Lord GOD says."

cards.question: True or false: when Ezekiel speaks God's words to Israel, God says that whoever refuses to listen, let him refuse.
